text:
deploy-bot: Canary deploy -> rollback executed for chart=payments-service v1.4.2 (digest: abc123def). Reason: 3xx/5xx spike on readiness checks in eu-west-1 canary. Rollback completed at 2026-03-21T09:00:00Z. Observed: 2 pods stuck in Terminating state after rollback. Release window open until 18:00 UTC. @maria tagging for manual cleanup and release note update 

maria: seeing the two Terminating pods on nodes node-eu-4 and node-eu-7. They have PVCs attached but PVC status looks Bound. Not sure if finalizers are blocking termination. Can someone coordinate safe cleanup? :eyes: 

jon: I can take node-eu-4 after I finish the backup job (10m). Quick check: "kubectl get pod -n payments payments-xxxxx -o yaml" to see finalizers & owner refs. If it's just kubelet stuck on mount, `kubectl delete pod --grace-period=0 --force` followed by `kubectl patch pvc <name> -p '{"metadata": {"finalizers":[]}}'` might do it. 

sam: prefer to avoid force-delete unless mount is stuck. Try removing the stuck finalizer on the Pod if it's a custom finalizer. Example: 
```bash
kubectl -n payments patch pod payments-xxxxx -p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":null}}' --type=merge
```
If that doesn't work, `sudo lsof /var/lib/kubelet/pods/<uid>` on node to see active mounts, but ops will need to assist.

adele: note for release notes: we should include a short explanation: "Rollback to payments-service v1.4.2 due to canary readiness spike; manual pod cleanup required for 2 canary pods; no migrations applied; customers unaffected." I'll draft and @maria can sign off. 

ops: I can SSH to node-eu-7 to check mounts in parallel. Heads-up: if we force-delete a pod with attached PV, the storage layer may need a detach; check CSI driver logs. Steps I recommend: 
1) Check pod finalizers/ownerrefs 
2) Attempt `kubectl describe pod` to surface events 
3) If kubelet has hung mounts, cordon node and drain non-critical pods OR restart kubelet after ensuring safe detachment.

maria: OK jon, please take node-eu-4. @ops please check node-eu-7. Sam, hold off on patch until we confirm no in-flight I/O. I'll run `kubectl describe pod payments-xxxxx -n payments` and paste events. 

jon: on node-eu-4 now. Events show: "FailedMount: timeout waiting for the volume to attach/mount" and last kubelet heartbeat was normal. Trying `kubectl delete pod payments-xxxxx -n payments --grace-period=30` now, will monitor CSI detach.

deploy-bot: Post-rollback healthcheck: payments-service frontend (eu-west-1) 1m rolling 5xx rate dropped to baseline. Alerting: none. 

ops: on node-eu-7 found leftover mount process from sidecar; killed process, executed `umount /var/lib/kubelet/pods/...` then signaled CSI detach. PVC shows `Released` then `Bound` again, looks healthy. 

jon: deletion succeeded, pod recreated on a healthy node and is Ready. I'll add the exact cleanup steps to the release notes (including the exact pod names and commands used). 

adele: thanks — draft release note line: "Rollback applied: payments-service pinned to v1.4.2 due to canary readiness regressions; two canary pods required manual cleanup (kubelet mount lock cleared; pods force-deleted gracefully); no customer impact. See internal postmortem link." Can we include the command snippet? 

maria: please redact node hostnames and internal trace IDs in public-facing release notes. For internal runbook include full commands. I'll update both. 

jon: internal runbook excerpt added to release doc: 
```bash
kubectl -n payments describe pod payments-xxxxx # check events
kubectl -n payments delete pod payments-xxxxx --grace-period=30 # allow kubelet to detach
# if stuck: ssh node && sudo systemctl restart kubelet OR kill mount blocker then umount
```

maria: I've updated the release notes (internal & public). Public blurb posted to release-notes repo. Internal doc updated with pod names and timestamps. Last check: 10m post-rollback all services in eu-west-1 are green. Closing thread unless regressions appear. :white_check_mark: 

deploy-bot: Canary/rollback thread closed by manual cleanup. Summary appended to incident log id=rlb-2026-03-21-009.
